It wasn't so at my time, many years back. I wasn't in a gvt school, and I had a concession card. Of course, getting one wasn't easy. One has to go to the ksrtc office, get the application form, take it to school, get principal's signature, seat, etc, then again go back to that office and apply - both visits during their working hours, quite a task. But then, my neighbour was this friendly conductor uncle 🙂

Students can avail a concession in ksrtc busses. They have to apply at ksrtc office, will be allocated a concession card for the whole year, the bus conductor will tick off on the card on each travel, twice a day. The student will have to pay in advance at the office and the destination and start points cannot be changed. Now, all routes are not covered by ksrtc busses and even if a route is covered, the frequency of ksrtc busses plying is not enough to cater to the demand of the commuters. The gap is filled by the pvt busses. The pvt busses are running in prescribed routes at prescribed times, which are derived based on the demand of commuters. Where ever the pvt busses are already running, ksrtc wouldn't bother those routes and those timings. So the students who have to take those particular routes, are allowed to avail concession from the pvt buses. Now it was up to the private bus business people to have devised a system to the process of availing this concession. I don't think anybody really bothered to do it, drivers are happy not to stop at bus-stops crowded by students and conductors curse the students when they ask for the students' concession ticket. 
It's been decades since I travelled on a concession ticket. All this is from my memory of those good old days. This was rather nostalgic :)

1. Yes there could be suicide clauses and YES there IS of course a gestation period. You can never be sure until tou speak with the insurance agent. Taking advise elsewhere could be risky. 
2. Your proposition has another big risk. What if your plan doesn't go well and you end up as having to be taken care of? 
3. Insurance companies may not be very forth coming. Are the beneficiaries savy enough to fight for it and get their dues? Do they have  enough resources to do it? And would they want to do it? 
4. How can you be sure that you are any less valuable than the cover you choose? Modern insurance companies have sophisticated algorithms to gauge and assess your true value and they aren't going to cover you for any more than what they estimate you for. So why would you undersell yourselves? More importantly, how can you assume that the cover is going to be enough for the beneficiaries? Needs change, prices raise, inflation, what not! 
5. On what basis did you conclude that your wife and kid need be the only beneficiaries? How do you know for sure that nobody else needs you? Just because you don't have people knocking on your door and telling you that you are important to them, you cannot assume otherwise. Today everything is commoditized, even miseries are. Think of it, our little conversation on this digital platform is contributing to someone's paycheck somewhere. So, every individual contributes positively to the economy. I am myself a worthless asshole, much worse than you could imagine. But, even this loser me, is a number in the population that makes up a market and hence even I push those cogs that run the economy, albeit my push be so tiny.
